sections.h2: What the Madison County Register of Deeds does
sections.html:
The office files your signed deed in the county's permanent index. That filing is the moment the transfer becomes visible to everyone else. The phone number is 828-649-3131.

The register checks the document, collects the fixed state fees and the seller's stamp tax, and notes the time of filing. Valuation and yearly billing happen down the road at Tax Administration in Marshall, which is open weekdays 8:00am to 5:00pm at 5707 Highway 25/70, Room 25.

Call the register before you travel and ask about current counter hours, or let your closing attorney handle the office from a distance. Plan a second call to Tax Administration too. A deed that is filed cleanly but never reaches the tax roll keeps sending the old owner a bill.

North Carolina ranks competing claims by when each was registered. Under G.S. 47-18, deeds, options, leases running beyond three years and rights of first refusal gain force against lien creditors and paying purchasers only once registered in the county where the land sits.

For a Madison County parcel, the Madison County office is the only one that counts, wherever the seller lives. Excise tax on a parcel spanning two counties is paid where more of the value lies.

  • A buyer whose deed waits unfiled can lose out to a creditor who files first.
  • A new lender's deed of trust filed late may rank behind liens that were never meant to come first.
  • A deed filed in a neighboring county leaves the Madison County record unchanged.

That is why closings end with the deed and the loan documents going in on the same day, in the order the attorney planned.

sections.h2: Recording fees at the Madison County counter
sections.html:
One statute, G.S. 161-10, sets the fees for every North Carolina county, so Madison County has no schedule of its own. A plain deed costs $26.00 up to 15 pages, and a deed of trust costs $64.00 up to 35 pages.

Madison County recording charges under G.S. 161-10
Document or serviceCharge
General instrument, up to 15 pages$26.00
General instrument, each extra page$4.00
Mortgage or deed of trust, up to 35 pages$64.00
Mortgage or deed of trust, each extra page$4.00
Plat, each sheet$21.00
Certified copy, page one$5.00
Certified copy, later pages$2.00 each
Release or cancellation of a mortgageFree

Two surcharges can apply: $25.00 for a document in nonstandard format and $10.00 for every extra instrument bundled into one filing. Payment is due before filing.

sections.h2: Does a land split need a recorded plat first?
sections.html:
Usually yes, when the split counts as a subdivision. The county's subdivision ordinance, revised June 28, 2022, bars the sale or transfer of any lot on a required subdivision plat until the final plat is recorded by the Register of Deeds.

The register is told not to file a subdivision plat that has not been approved under the ordinance. A building permit or septic permit also has to wait until the Planning Board approves the final plat and the register records it. Buyers of a back lot get caught here, since a lender will not close on a parcel that cannot be permitted.

  • Combining or recombining recorded lots without adding lots is carved out, as long as the results meet county standards.
  • A family subdivision has its own approval, and the final plat carries a title block that says so.
  • Plats must comply with G.S. 47-30 to be suitable for recording.

An owner may sign contracts to sell by reference to an approved preliminary plat before the final plat exists, though the lot itself cannot transfer until that plat is recorded. If you plan to carve a lot off a Madison County tract, ask the county's subdivision administrator whether your split needs a plat, and settle it before you list.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed stamp tax
sections.html:
The seller. G.S. 105-228.30 sets a levy of $1.00 per $500 of price, counting any fraction of $500 as a full unit, on whoever transfers the land. The register takes the money before the deed is entered.

Half stays with the county. Monthly remittances carry the other half to the Department of Revenue, less a 2 percent county share of it.

The exact figure appears on your settlement statement, next to the loan payoff and any tax balance. A cash purchase works the same way.

sections.h2: Email alerts when a document is filed
sections.html:
The register has offered an email notice whenever a recorded document matches a name an owner signed up to watch. Sign-up asks for your name, your email and the names to monitor, followed by a confirmation email that may land in a junk folder.

If you own land you rarely visit, or you are settling an estate, an alert like this can catch a forged deed or a stray lien the day it reaches the index. Call 828-649-3131 to confirm the service is running.

Electronic filing is a separate question for the same counter. Your closing attorney knows which vendors the office accepts.

sections.h2: After the sale: the two Marshall offices
sections.html:
Filing the deed hands the assessor the new owner. That office tracks ownership changes and keeps the property maps.

  • After recording, call Tax Administration at 828-649-0734 and confirm the owner name.
  • Have the year's September 1 bill paid or credited at closing so the lien does not follow the house.
  • Where a circuit breaker deferral exists, give the tax office 10 days to prepare deferred bills.
  • Take the parcel number from the tax bill and put it on the deed paperwork.

The county counted 11,874 housing units in 2025, with 77.5 percent owner-occupied across 2020 to 2024. Ordinary sales and family transfers make up most of what the register sees.

sections.h2: What to have ready before closing
sections.html:
A title agent or attorney files the paperwork. Gather these items so nothing stalls.

  • The old deed, so names can be copied exactly.
  • Payoff statements for each deed of trust on the parcel. Lenders then file cancellations, and those carry no fee.
  • The parcel number, plus a survey if the acreage is uncertain.
  • For an inherited house, estate paperwork. Small estate affidavits go to the superior court clerk, and G.S. 28A-25-1 sets the dollar limits.

A cash buyer can take a house with a tangled history, yet every link in the chain still has to be recorded properly. Running the title early gives you time to chase down a missing release before the closing date.

If the closing is by mail or through a remote attorney, ask who carries the deed to the office and who confirms the recording afterward. Keep the book and page reference once the office gives it to you, because the next buyer's title search will start from it.

faqs.q: What number reaches the Madison County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Call 828-649-3131. Ask about counter hours and recording options before you send anything.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Madison County?
faqs.a: A deed of 15 pages or fewer costs $26.00, then $4.00 per added page. Mortgages and deeds of trust cost $64.00 through page 35. State law fixes both amounts.

faqs.q: Who pays the Madison County excise tax?
faqs.a: The seller pays, at $1.00 per $500 of price, and the register collects it before recording.

faqs.q: Does Madison County charge to file a mortgage release?
faqs.a: No. G.S. 161-10 sets no charge for filing a satisfaction or cancellation.

faqs.q: After recording, who updates the tax bill owner?
faqs.a: The assessor tracks ownership changes, so confirm the new name with Tax Administration and settle the September 1 bill at closing.
